subject: ventures/well-pump-bid-calculator
professional: an owner-operator of a well-service / pump-installation shop (licensed pump installer) who bids pump pulls and pressure-tank swaps every week; first checks: is drop pipe, wire gauge and tank sizing in the takeoff, and does the margin math hold

evidence.correctness: Ran calculateBid (node) on 3 configurations with the page's own default rates and recomputed each independently in Python (labor = hours x wage x 1.32; overhead on direct cost; price = cost / (1 - margin)). (1) 120 ft 3/4 HP + new tank + good pitless: 5.17 h, labor $286.62, material $790.50, cost $1,371.31, price $2,109.70, both match. (2) 280 ft 1.5 HP seized pitless, stuck pump, VFD, 300 ft cable: 13.5 h, cost $3,844.96, price $5,915.32, match. (3) 40 ft jet, pump-only, proposed $1,495: 2.75 h, cost $539.80, price $830.47, proposed margin 63.9%, match. Also hand-checked the 60 ft preset ($1,176.2) and the 40 ft jet + tank preset ($1,584.7) against the numbers printed on the how-much-to-charge page: match. Limit: the formulas are the author's own method (margin on price, overhead on direct cost is standard job-costing), and there is no external standard for pump-swap prices. Starting rates are ballpark and plausible against typical US shop pricing (1/2 HP submersible $280, 1.5 HP $780, tank $280, ~3.75 h for a shallow swap); not verifiable to a source. No hydraulics (TDH, drawdown, tank sizing) is computed, so there was nothing to check there.
evidence.completeness: README features checked by running: pump type/HP/work/pitless presets (calc.mjs suggested*Kit), extra footage clamped to zero for a shallow well, loaded labor, price = cost/(1-margin), price per foot, effective hourly rate, hour split, walk-away price, proposed-price scoring, copy bid summary: all work (119 tests pass). Also ships proposal.mjs (proposal text), share.mjs (share link), usage.mjs (opt-out counter) and 3 SEO pages. No stubs or TODOs found in the .mjs files. VENTURE.yaml stage is prototype, all hypotheses untested. I did not drive the page in a real browser; page.test.mjs (8 tests) passed.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the venture directory: 119 pass, 0 fail, 0.5 s. Seeded 3 mutations in calc.mjs, reverted each by git checkout (git status clean afterwards): (a) overhead applied to direct cost minus travel: 2 tests failed; (b) extra cable off by one foot (includedCableFeet + 1): 2 failed; (c) hoist fee charged for jet instead of submersible: 4 failed. All caught. Tests are example-based with fixed expected numbers, no property tests, no check against an independent calculation.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs in full (407 lines), skimmed proposal.mjs and share.mjs structure. calc.mjs is pure, input-validated with named errors, rejects margin >= 100, clamps extra footage. Defects: the hp input is validated but never used in arithmetic (pump cost comes from the page's preset, so calling calculateBid with hp only changes a label); the jet job still takes cable feet and a cable cost line (irrelevant to a jet pump, harmless because the preset keeps it under the included run); index.html is a 49 KB single file with defaults duplicated from calc.mjs (the preset tables live in both places). No unhandled-input crash found.
evidence.claims: Checked: README privacy (localStorage only, usage.mjs, DNT/GPC) backed by usage.mjs and tests; disclaimer present in README and index.html; $1,176 / $2,110 / $5,915 / $1,585 figures on the SEO page all reproduce. Defects: the index.html FAQ says material is '57.6% of direct cost against labor's 20.9%', but those are shares of total cost incl. overhead (material is 68.0% of direct cost, labor 24.7%), so the sentence is wrong as written. llms.txt links all four pages to the old github.io host, while README and VENTURE.yaml give https://marisstella.app/well-pump-bid-calculator/ as the live address (CLAUDE.md says the old address now only redirects). README step 1 says horsepower matters, but the engine ignores it. The 'walk-away price' is total cost including overhead and the stated margin target is zero-profit-free; the page explains it.
evidence.fitness: Walked a 280 ft 1.5 HP seized-pitless pull through the engine and the page: a shop gets a price, margin, hour split and a customer-facing text draft in a minute. But the user must supply nearly 30 rates, and the takeoff leaves out things a shop would add by hand: drop pipe / torque arrestor / safety rope material, wire splice kit, pressure switch gauge set, check valves, disposal. For the deep job the extra 180 ft of drop pipe is priced as labor only. Usable as a sanity check, not as a complete bid sheet. No usage evidence (hypotheses untested).
evidence.domain: Compared against normal pump-installer takeoff practice and NGWA / manufacturer sizing practice. Sound: pitless and stuck-pull as separate hour lines, margin as share of price, VFD / constant-pressure as an option, jet vs submersible split. Departs: (1) no drop-pipe material cost per foot, the biggest depth-driven material on a deep well; (2) cable is a single $1.85/ft rate, but a 1.5 HP pump at 300 ft needs heavier gauge (10 AWG or larger) so the cost is understated for exactly the deep jobs it targets; (3) no pressure tank sizing or drawdown (gallons per cycle, pump GPM x 1 min rule, cut-in/cut-out) so 'new tank' is one flat $280 whatever the pump; (4) HP choices stop at 1.5, no 2/3/5 HP or 3-wire vs 2-wire; (5) no depth-to-water or TDH check that the chosen pump can actually lift at that depth. A pump installer would accept the margin math and distrust the materials.

defects.what: No drop-pipe material cost: extra drop-pipe footage is billed only as labor (hoursPerExtraFoot), so a 280 ft well omits ~180 ft of pipe, torque arrestor and rope, understating the deep-job price.
Cable priced at one flat per-foot rate regardless of pump HP and run length; heavier gauge needed for 1.5 HP at 300 ft costs more.
No pressure-tank sizing or drawdown logic, no TDH or lift check; the tank is one flat cost and the pump HP is chosen without any hydraulic check.
FAQ says material is 57.6% of 'direct cost' and labor 20.9%; those are shares of total cost incl. overhead (68.0% and 24.7% of direct cost).
llms.txt page links use the old github.io host instead of https://marisstella.app/well-pump-bid-calculator/.
hp input is validated but unused in the arithmetic; only changes a label in the summary.

verdict: Arithmetic is right and well tested: three configurations recomputed independently matched to the cent, the page's published figures reproduce, 119 tests pass and all three seeded mutations were caught. It does not meet the bar because claims scores 2 (a mislabelled percentage in the FAQ and stale hosts in llms.txt) and the domain scores 2: a pump installer would find the margin and hour-splitting method sensible but miss drop-pipe material, wire gauge by HP and run, and tank sizing, so the deep-well jobs it targets come out low on materials. It is finished against its own README (completeness 3) and a decent prototype for a sanity check, not yet a complete bid sheet.
